children: Bernstein cut its price target on Alibaba Group Holding
to $165 from $180, citing investor concerns surrounding the company's recent $10.2 billion equity raise, while keeping its Buy rating.

Analyst Robin Zhu said the fundraising has raised questions because Alibaba held more than $30 billion in net cash when it accessed the market. The transaction has also prompted investors to reassess the expected returns from the company's heavy investment program.

Zhu's revised estimates factor in higher server costs and rental rates, while projecting stronger revenue from Alibaba's non-AI cloud operations. His valuation considers the company's e-commerce and cloud businesses separately and also compares the result with a forward earnings multiple.

Still, Bernstein sees potential for Alibaba's AI infrastructure spending to generate returns. The Zhenwu 810E chip is estimated to reach payback in about three years, while the newer M890 could do so in roughly 2.5 years.
The lower target could pressure sentiment, although AI-related cloud growth may offer support.

title: Veteran Analyst Delivers Stark Warning on Alibaba Stock
